articleTitle: Array Tilt Angles to Maximize Solar Power Generation Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Each summer in Pakistan, the country faces dark nights without power, especially during intense heat waves. This is due to increased electricity demand for air conditioners and agricultural needs, leading to a power shortage with no strategy for managing peak demand during the summer. The increased daytime electricity demand and resulting load-shedding crisis exacerbate the situation. To cope, most electricity consumers in Pakistan use photovoltaic (PV) systems for their daily needs. However, 99% of these PV systems are set at fixed tilt angles, typically aligned with the location’s latitude. This general approach results in lower electricity output, particularly during extreme weather conditions—both scorching summers and cold winters when power demand is highest. This research aims to identify the ideal tilt angle for PV systems across all provinces of Pakistan, determining separate angles for summer and winter to better meet peak demands in extreme weather. By doing so, the study seeks to reduce reliance on conventional energy sources and promote cleaner, greener power generation. The concept also maximizes irradiation and power density, optimizing the use of available rooftop or land space. The research compares PV power generation at a fixed angle with low tilt angles for summer and high tilt angles for winter across various provincial zones in Pakistan. Findings show that at a 12° tilt angle in the summer, power generation is higher than at a fixed angle, while a high tilt angle of 48° in winter is suitable to meet peak electricity loads.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of a Photovoltaic-based Reliable Street Lighting System using PVSyst Software
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: As conventional fossil fuels run out and their environmental effects worsen, renewable energy sources like photovoltaic (PV) energy are becoming more and more popular as clean, sustainable electricity sources, and shortage of power in Pakistan and excess load shedding is increasing day by day. The kind of photovoltaic modules, the potential for solar radiation, and the location all affect how well photovoltaic systems work. This study, a standalone solar PV system that powers a clean and green energy-efficient street lighting system is designed and simulated using PVsyst simulation software. The simulation is run to examine the standalone PV system’s monthly/annual energy generation (kWh) and output power for street lights in the Institute of Southern Punjab Multan. Additionally, the system has various battery and solar losses. For the standalone PV system, three parallel strings with two series-connected Solar model PV-TE120MF5N of 120 Wp solar cell modules are utilized. To power the system throughout the night, a total of 12 lead acid tubular batteries with a voltage of 24 volts and a capacity of 3450 Ah are needed. These batteries are part of the OPzS solar 4600 battery type. According to the modeling findings, the yearly output of specific energy and total available energy was determined to be 1306 kWh/kWp and 940.6 kWh respectively. Battery aging depends on the state of wear which depends on the cycle and static state, according to the simulation proposed battery wear on the cycle is 99.1%, and in the static state 80.0% and the battery lifetime is 5 years. Performance ratio (PR) data shows that the greatest PR for the proposed PV system was 73.5% in January, the lowest PR for the system was 43.8% in September, and the average PR for the system over the course of a year was 54.7%. Following the identification of the primary cause of energy losses, the loss diagrams computed and displayed the specific losses for the entire year. The suggested system’s cost-effectiveness was assessed using a straightforward payback time computation.

articleTitle: IoRT enabled gesture mimicking Robotic Hand based on Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Human Robot Interaction (HRI) is a multi-model, progressive approach where humans get together with robots to complement one another. The Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT) happens to be an intriguing technology of the modern world, but it becomes immersive when combined with computer vision. IoRT refers to the control of robots over the internet. According to the International Labor Organization (ILO), close to 3 million people die each year due to occupational hazards. Explosives, munition, chemical processing, and mining industries are in the midst of pernicious industries. This paper presents a human gesture-controlled robotic hand that uses MediaPipe and OpenCV libraries to classify gestures and proposes an IoRT architecture. The Cortex M0+ based Raspberry Pi Pico MCU has been used to realize the concept of AI on embedded systems where a worker makes a robotic entity to mimic him while sitting in a safe cabin, eliminating the need for numerous sensors and cumbersome wearables.

articleTitle: Towards a Time Series Prediction of Air Quality Index
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Air pollution has become an important topic due to its impact on the lives of millions of people. Much research is being undertaken to ensure that air pollution levels are contained within manageable levels as high levels can lead to severe repercussions on health. In this research, Dalat City of Vietnam has been studied and we consider different sensors for the trajectory of pollutants and Air Quality Index (AQI) of the city. Multiple time series algorithms have been used to predict the time series values of the pollutants and AQI. A cross model was developed, to establish the relationship between AQI and the presence of different objects on the road such as buses and motorcycles. The objects were identified by using Yolov5 algorithm and subsequently, linear regression was run to determine the relationship between the objects identified and the respective AQI levels. The linear regression had R square of 0.436. The best Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) for air pollutants was determined by Sensor 3 and AQI by Sensor 8.

articleTitle: A Modular Distributed Operating System Architecture for Scalable Mesh Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Operating systems mediate user-device interactions, crucially managing resources, software execution, and application interfaces. In the face of technological advancements, the demand for secure, resilient, and scalable operating systems grows. This paper introduces a novel modular and decentralized operating system architecture, emphasizing robustness, scalability, and advanced parallel processing. The proposed mesh architecture diverges from conventional kernel designs, distributing responsibilities across nodes to eliminate a central point of failure, enhancing scalability and fortifying fault tolerance. The study advocates for a mesh-based operating system adaptable to diverse microprocessor platforms.

articleTitle: Ensuring Child Safety: An IoT-Based Surveillance System for Remote Monitoring and Detection of Anomalous Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Amidst the economic pressures compelling many families to juggle multiple jobs, the ability to maintain consistent parental care for children diminishes. Yet, it remains essential that families feel assured their children are safe in their absence. Addressing these concerns, our research proposes an Internet of Things (IoT) surveillance system with real-time video and audio monitoring capabilities. This system detects anomalies such as crying, movement beyond camera range, and potential signs of child abuse, notifying connected devices with alerts tailored to the severity of the situation. A robust Artificial Intelligence model has been configured to map out the poses of the caretaker and child to detect any signs of abuse and stress. Parents and other concerned adults can monitor their children remotely using our system.

Author Keywords: Image processing Object detection Pose recognition Edge computing

articleTitle: Optimized Sizing of Grid Connected PV Systems for Distributed Generation in Remote Sindh and Balochistan
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: The grid-connected photovoltaic system (GCPVS) is a practical technology for Distributed generation (DG), addressing energy crises in remote areas. This research evaluates the economic feasibility and solar energy potential in Sindh and Balochistan, Pakistan. Findings indicate sufficient solar radiation in Sindh’s remote areas, with optimized tilt angles enhancing solar generation. DG options like PV systems can mitigate voltage dips and load shedding, especially in remote areas with long distribution lines. With 31,389 villages lacking power, these DG systems are vital for Sindh and Balochistan. The study shows a high-performance ratio (PR) for proposed sites, aiding Pakistan’s government in implementing GCPVS in isolated regions.

articleTitle: Critical analysis of resource sharing and optimization in fog clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Fog computing aims to process data closer to its source to reduce latency and enhance application performance. However, the integration of an additional fog layer introduces complexities in resource management and service guarantees. This paper critically analyzes resource sharing and optimization in fog clustering, focusing on adaptive middleware designed to manage resources within and across fog clusters. We present a novel middleware architecture that facilitates efficient load balancing, task scheduling, and inter-cluster communication. The middleware’s performance is evaluated through simulations using OMNeTH++, highlighting improvements in response time and resource utilization compared to traditional cloud processing.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Poet Attribution model for Punjabi Poetry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Poetry is a profound medium for expressing emotions and beliefs, with South Asian languages like Urdu, Hindi, and Punjabi boasting rich poetic traditions. The digital age and the rise of social media have amplified the visibility of these poetic works but also heightened instances of plagiarism and misattribution. In this paper, we present a Deep Learning model for Poet Attribution for Punjabi poetry using Shahmukhi, Gurmukhi, and Roman scripts. Our dataset consists of 830 poems from 11 different poets. We utilize Multilingual DistilBERT to generate the embedding of each poem in the 768-dimensional vector space. By conducting extensive experiments and utilizing advanced approaches, including Bi-LSTM and Bi-GRU we obtained a test accuracy of $91.57 \%$ on the Roman script. Additionally, we achieved accuracies of $90.36 \%$ and $87.95 \%$ on the Gurmukhi and Shahmukhi scripts, respectively.

articleTitle: Bagging as Defence Mechanism Against Adversarial Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: With the gaining popularity of Artificial intelligence and its adoption by organizations in their day-to-day business operations, it is becoming increasingly important to defend machine learning architectures from attackers (adversaries) that tend to exploit model predictions for their benefit. Bootstrap aggregation or Bagging has proven its effectiveness against various adversarial attacks by making use of its majority voting mechanism making model predictions more robust to noise during training and testing. Recent studies are more focused on techniques to increase model robustness and evaluate performance via sample-wise or collective robustness certificates where the aim is to certify the minimum number of robust predictions guaranteed by the model [1]. In this research, an architecture for multi-layered defense strategy against adversarial attacks is proposed. The proposed architecture introduces bagging with adversarial training, gradient masking, detection & filtering. Initially, the model undergoes adversarial training using the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) to generate and incorporate adversarial samples, thereby creating an extended training dataset. A dedicated deep neural network, trained solely on clean data, subsequently screens this dataset to detect and remove potentially poisoned samples. The sanitized dataset is then partitioned using hash-based sampling into subsets, each fed to a sub-classifier equipped with gradient masking techniques including gradient clipping, noise addition, and non-differentiable layers to obscure useful gradient information from potential attackers. Finally, an ensemble of these sub-classifiers employs majority voting to deliver robust predictions. This structured approach not only enhances the model’s resilience to adversarial inputs but also maintains consistency and reliability in adversarial environments. To demonstrate our work, we use the CIFAR10 dataset and evaluate its robustness. We are able to achieve a robust accuracy of 77.47% on the CIFAR10 dataset outperforming many complex approaches on robust adversarial accuracy. It is important to mention that the proposed architecture does also consider other forms of adversarial attacks including data poisoning, label poisoning, and model extraction attacking techniques. Code is available: https://github.com/mahadahmed786/bagging-against-adversarial-attacks.

articleTitle: Adopting Long-Short Term Memory to predict reliability in different use cases in autonomous vehicles in 6G
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: In vehicular networks, reliability is a critical problem. This study suggests applying Deep Learning (DL) to automatically predict the reliability of vehicular networks including different types of components. First, a data set is generated using simulation parameters from our previous work. Next, a framework is proposed that use the deep learning method, Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) to predict the networks’ reliability. The performance is compared with other machine learning techniques. The results showed, the proposed model outperforms other machine learning methods for reliability prediction. The performance is also evaluated excluding driver’s behavior and reaction. The results indicate that the reliability of the system decreases by $10 \%$. Further, the performance was also evaluated excluding Prime Reliability Factor (PRF), code rate and coding. According to the results, reliability decreased by $3 \%$ more.

articleTitle: Study on the Impact of AI-powered Green Supply Chain Management Practices on Organizational Sustainable Performance with the mediation role of Technology Innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI)–powered green supply chain management (GSCM) practices on sustainable performance in the Pakistani technology industry. A key focus is placed on the mediating role of technology innovation, which is crucial in driving the industry forward. A quantitative research design was employed, utilizing survey data from 540 supply chain managers and executives. Structural equation modeling revealed that AI-powered GSCM practices significantly influence both technology innovation and sustainable performance. The findings underscore the pivotal role of technology innovation in the industry’s progress and offer valuable insights for managers and policymakers seeking to leverage AI for achieving both economic and environmental goals.

articleTitle: Distributed Estimation of Anomalies using a Low Complexity PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Any wireless sensor network can experience anomalies that can hinder performance. This work presents a distributed estimation algorithm that estimates any such anomalies using a PSO algorithm. PSO algorithms are computationally expensive. This work presents a low complexity version of the algorithm that removes redundant computations and achieves excellent performance as well. Low complexity algorithms are essential for a longer battery life of wireless sensor so this algorithm provides an excellent alternative to the basic linear adaptive filtering algorithms that have low complexity but require a lot more time to achieve similar results.

articleTitle: Optimizing Membrane Distillation Configuration for Superior Heat and Mass Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Membrane distillation (MD) has emerged as a promising technique for desalination and water purification, offering potential advantages in terms of energy efficiency and operational flexibility. However, challenges related to heat and mass transfer inefficiencies limit its widespread adoption. This study explores the use of innovative materials and optimized configurations to enhance heat and mass transfer in direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD) systems. By integrating advanced hybrid membranes with nano-coating techniques and evaluating their performance through simulation-based methodologies, we demonstrate significant improvements in thermal conductivity, mass transfer efficiency, and fouling resistance. The results indicate that the newly developed hybrid membranes not only enhance heat and mass transfer rates but also maintain high separation efficiency, ultimately leading to improved overall system performance. These findings provide a foundation for the further development of MD technologies and suggest pathways for overcoming existing limitations, paving the way for more sustainable and efficient water treatment solutions.

articleTitle: Design of a Digital Twin Based Feedback Controller for a Parallel Mechanism Based Six Degree of Freedom Machining Bed
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: With the development of current technology, the process of removing material from a workpiece has become much more advanced. While these developments make it possible to remove material more quickly, they frequently compromise the workpiece’s accuracy and precision. This research suggests a six-degree-of-freedom machining bed that is based on a parallel mechanism—more precisely, a Stewart Platform—in contrast to conventional machining methods. The goal of the study is to provide a digital twin-based framework for this machining bed’s autonomous feedback control. The machining bed’s feedback controller is designed employing digital twin-based technology. The controller design and digital twin implementation can be carried out remotely and offline, apart from the physical twin and real-time controller, by utilizing an asynchronous link with adjustable time delays. This combination of feedback response and digital twin consistently reduces errors and improves stability.

articleTitle: Development of a novel OMNET++ framework for analysis of an NB-IoT uplink network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: In this paper, we have presented the development of a novel narrowband-IoT (NB-IoT) simulation framework using event driven simulator, OMNET++. NB-IoT as a cellular technology finds promising potential in massive machine-type-communication (mMTC) use cases but unfortunately there is a lack of evaluation resources for such network deployments. Our implemented simulation framework can be used to effectively evaluate uplink network performance of NB-IoT networks. Moreover, we have considered mobility model in our framework to assess the effect of mobility of NB-IoT nodes on the network performance. We have presented the feature details of our developed framework and showcased some of the results obtained using this framework. Our framework is extendable to include advance features of NB-IoT as standardized in later 3GPP releases as well as incorporate different network and environment conditions to gauge its uplink performance.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning based Approach for Sindhi Poet Classification using Couplets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Sindhi poetry serves as a monument to the cultural richness of Sindhi heritage, encompassing themes of affection, dedication, and community harmony. However, the contemporary decline in Sindhi language usage calls for innovative preservation efforts. In this study, we present a Deep Learning-based model for the automatic classification of Sindhi poets based on couplets. The dataset consists of 3000 couplets authored by five well-known Sindhi poets, each representing distinct periods and subject styles. We utilize PySpark’s Word2Vec, a pre-trained BERT-based model called MuRIL, and Keras’s Embedding Layer to produce sentence-level embeddings for each couplet. By doing extensive experiments and utilizing advanced approaches including Stochastic Gradient Descent, Random Forest, and 1D Convolutional Neural Networks, we have achieved a test accuracy of 87.2%. Our study is the first to focus on Sindhi poetry, as to the best of our knowledge, no prior work has been done in this field.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Approaches for Animal Pose Estimation (APE): A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Animal pose estimation aims to detect the body parts and joints of animal to form a basic skeleton, on the basis of data collected in the form of images and annotations. Recently interest in animal pose estimation has increased after the success of research in Human Pose estimation, the main reasons being scientific investigation in the form of noninvasive behavioral tracking. In this paper, we present a survey on current deep learning methodologies animal pose estimation in single image or sequence of images. Although, the recently developed deep learning-based solutions have achieved high performance in human pose estimation, there still remain challenges for animal pose estimation due to a different body structure, lack of training data, and many other reasons. This work attempts to create a taxonomy that summarizes important aspects of deep learning for approaching the problem of Animal Pose with new vigor. We shall review the details of the proposed architectures, the main datasets, approaches, backbone architecture and measurement metrics. It is proposed to discuss and summarize the main methods proposed so far with particular interest on how deep learning models are used in animal pose estimation, discussing their main features and identify opportunities and challenges for future research.

articleTitle: Predicting Lung Cancer Recurrence Using a Mobile Application Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: It is a well-known fact that globally, lung cancer is the major issue that causes number of people to expire; this is due to the fact of its recurrence that is an important concern for those who have survived it. This article presents a mobile app framework which uses past medical records and chest X-ray images to predict possible reoccurrence of lung cancer. The framework includes elements such as data preparation, transfer learning through image classifiers, and CDC-Net which is a specialized model. Users interact with the app by carrying out self-assessments and entering their medical history. This information undergoes standardization or processing particularly for radiographic pictures like chest x -rays. Specifically, categorizes datasets are used in training the Chest Disease Classification Network model to determine whether there is a danger of another outbreak taking place or not. The app gives personalized predictions such as a likelihood ratio for return and provides medical advice along with preventive steps based on the findings presented herein. The strategy seeks to educate users on how to manage their own health effectively.

articleTitle: Hybrid Forecasting Model for Smart Grid Using Exogenous Variables
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: Smart grids augment the existing power grids with information and communication technology to enable enhanced monitoring and control. Power grid resilience and failure management have always been problems that have intrigued researchers and policymakers, who want to ensure the services offered are up to the mark and consumers can rely on the system. To improve the quality of service, data analytics, and forecasting can help with predictive analytics. Forecasting in smart grids can ensure that the optimal relationship between power generation and consumption can be optimized effectively. Hybrid forecasting, including multi-criteria forecasting, has shown promising results. In this paper, we outline exogenous variables from weather data that can be used in real-time hybrid forecasting of the smart grid in an energy management system. The framework presented in this work presents a base model for enhancing the quality of service in smart grid forecasting.

articleTitle: Effect of Cotton Dust Morphology on Photovoltaic Module Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: The use of renewable energy is increasing due to the high cost of conventional fuels and climate issues. Textile industries, specifically in Asian region, are shifting towards large PV plants in order to acquire cheap and clean energy. However, cotton dust presence in the textile mill environment causes performance issues for PV modules. This study examines the cotton dust particle effect on PV module by employing an experimental methodology. An indoor experimental setup is utilized to test the PV modules in two schemes, that are clean and dusty. The experiment is conducted for eight days with an hourly interval. It is observed that PV power output reduces significantly up to 15% in eight days as compared to clean PV module. The deposited cotton dust particles are also physically examined through compound microscope in order to determine its physical nature. It is being observed that cotton particles are composed of long, smooth fibers with irregular shapes. The particles are highly influenced by humidity, and their own high content of cellulose makes them vulnerable to stick on the PV surface and forming clumps and aggleromates that develop the hotspots on the PV surface. Along with that, as time progresses the cotton dust opaqueness also increases, ultimately reducing the transmittance and decreasing PV module performance. This study helps to devise a unique cleaning patterns and methods for textile units to enhance performance output.

articleTitle: Classification of Gastrointestinal Endoscopic Images Using Feature Space Particle Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Smart Technologies (ICETST)
abstract: The gastrointestinal tract is one of the most important parts of the digestive system. Its main functions include digestion, absorption of nutrients and excretion of waste materials, all of which are essential for a healthy human being. Huge number of people suffer from diseases related to the gastrointestinal tract which greatly affect their quality of life and can prove to be fatal. For this reason, it is important to identify these diseases at an early stage so that they can be appropriately treated. The gastrointestinal tract is examined by doing a procedure called endoscopy. During the procedure of endoscopy, abnormalities can sometimes be missed by gastroenterologists if they are in the early stages or if they are too minor. Therefore, in this study a robust and accurate mechanism is developed to correctly identify gastrointestinal abnormalities from endoscopic images. Feature space particle inference (FSPI) on neural network ensembles is used to create a model that is robust and accurate. In this ensemble model, each particle learns different features and then the predictions are combined. Thereby making it more robust. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, experiments are conducted on a well known KVASIR dataset.An accuracy of 96% and precision of 90% is achieved which is a considerable improvement from current state-of-the-art. The multi-view of the data is exploited in this way, by using feature-space inference instead of weight-space inference that is usually used in deep learning ensemble networks, to create more robust models and avoid over-parameterization.
